steps.description: Design and execute a numerical experiment to test the Landau Phase Transition Hypothesis on solution space rigidity. We will generate a system of analytic constraints (e.g., polynomial equations or differential constraints), train small feedforward networks of varying hidden widths $w$ to satisfy them, and measure the minimal width $N_c(w)$ required to achieve zero violation ($\max |error| \le 1e^{-3}$) on held-out constraints. The goal is to observe if $N_c(w)$ exhibits a sharp transition (rigid) or remains unattainable (fat) as $w$ increases. We will implement the training loop, constraint generator, and width scanner in Python (using PyTorch or JAX).

plans.objective: I select **[DIM: Computation] The Kolmogorov Complexity Hypothesis** as the primary candidate for the next iteration because it offers the sharpest numerical distinction (linear vs. constant/log) and is grounded in the fundamental algebraic structure of the constraints (rank of the constraint matrix), which is less dependent on the specific optimization dynamics (which can be noisy). If the constraints form a system of equations, the width required to satisfy them linearly with the count is a robust, checkable baseline.

steps.description: [auto-routed: surprise=1.00] Create a Python script to numerically test the Kolmogorov Complexity Hypothesis on a synthetic linear constraint system. The script will: (1) generate a linear system with rank r (representing rigid constraints) and w samples; (2) train small feedforward networks of varying hidden widths N; (3) evaluate out-of-sample error on held-out points; (4) determine N_c(w) as the minimum width achieving max absolute error ≤ 1e-3; (5) scan N_c across increasing w to check if it remains bounded (rigid) or grows (fat). Output will be saved to `/workspace/research_outputs/shusheng_rsi_run53/kolmogorov_scan_results.json`.

Implement the algebraic rigidity hypothesis as a Python script that defines a family of analytic constraints (e.g., polynomial identities on a grid), varies the number of constraints w, sweeps hidden layer width N, and records the minimum N achieving zero violation (max abs error ≤ 1e-3) on a held-out test set. The script will output N_c(w) values and a trend plot to determine rigidity (small finite N_c independent of w) vs. fatness. No external simulation tools are needed; this is a pure ML/math experiment.
